candidate.title: hiCLIP
candidate.scope: The middle hiCLIP row of the assigned Illumina poster: RNA hybrid and individual-nucleotide resolution ultraviolet crosslinking and immunoprecipitation, interpreted at schematic scope using the original STAU1 implementation. Both explicitly drawn Same RNA and Different RNA substrate origins and mapping outcomes are retained. They are alternative RNA topologies passing through one shared illustrated workflow, not independent drawn processing lanes, a pooling operation, or separate named methods. The adjacent PIP-Seq and RBNS rows and the partial chemical panel at the right are outside this card. iCLIP supplies the named cDNA-library component, not an alternative target. The verified collection page 63 is a secondary hiCLIP catalogue match; references clarify this row without adding unshown adaptations.

The primary demonstration concerns STAU1-bound RNA in human cells; the poster uses a generic RBP icon.

operations.label: UV 254 nm
operations.description: Irradiate the RBP-bound RNA input to capture protein-RNA contacts. The output is an RNA-protein cross-linked complex; either depicted input topology follows this route.
operations.mechanism: UV-C protein-RNA cross-linking, as identified by the primary hiCLIP schematic.
operations.information_effect: Preserves the in vivo RBP-RNA association used to enrich the biological target.

operations.label: Partial RNase digestion
operations.description: Partially digest exposed RNA in the cross-linked material. Unprotected sections are cut, leaving shortened duplex-associated RNA fragments with the RBP.
operations.mechanism: The paper identifies RNase I digestion after cell lysis; lysis is contextual preparation, not a separate block drawn in the hiCLIP row.
operations.information_effect: Removes unprotected sequence while retaining the depicted local duplex association; same- versus different-RNA origin is not yet a sequence-level association.

method_scopes.rationale: All listed operations belong to the one arrowed hiCLIP row and apply to its alternative same- and different-RNA origins. Shared post-digestion states retain either origin and never assert mixing. The primary paper explicitly describes both mapping outcomes and resolves the two adaptor end types. The broad Sequence caption is decomposed only at the necessary RNA-to-cDNA-to-read interface, supported by the primary figure caption. STAU1 demonstrates this architecture within the hiCLIP method; the poster does not establish identical capture conditions for every possible RBP implementation.
